title: Converge SLI definitions and tracing golden-signatures for console analytics pipeline
creator: Jamie Park
description:
Goal: create a single, unambiguous SLI/SLO catalog for the console analytics ingestion path and define a small set of "golden trace" signatures that represent healthy and unhealthy behavior. Scope covers the metrics and tracing signals emitted by the ingestion front-end, routing layer, transformation workers, and the write-to-store step.

Why now: multiple teams own telemetry for analytics and we see drift in alert thresholds, duplicate dashboards, and false-positive incidents. This work reduces fatigue, improves on-call actionability, and enables more accurate cost-vs-latency tradeoffs for batching and KV-cache heuristics.

Deliverables:
- Canonical SLI document (latency p50/p90/p99, request success rate, data completeness, processing lag per-tenant) with concrete query specs for the monitoring backend.
- A set of 4 golden-trace patterns (healthy ingest, transient backpressure, persistent slow-path, malformed payload spikes) encoded as example traces + span semantics.
- Trace-based anomaly detection knobs (signature matching + a small similarity score) and recommended sampling rules.
- Updated Grafana dashboards and a condensed on-call view for quick TTR.
- Runbook and playbooks that map SLO breaches to next actions and targeted mitigations (e.g., route to cheaper model variant, enable prefix KV-cache).

Non-goals: instrumenting downstream analytics consumers (outside of ingestion pipeline), or changing storage schema. Those are separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: SLI catalog published in docs/confluence with exact monitoring queries and ownership
At least 4 golden-trace examples uploaded to tracing service and referenced in the SLI doc
Trace sampling config implemented for ingestion service (config + rollout PR merged)
New Grafana dashboard 'Analytics Ingest — Oncall Summary' created and linked from console runbooks
Synthetic ingestion probe added to CI that emits the golden-trace and validates it via trace assertions
Runbook updated with step-by-step mitigation steps for each SLI category and one postmortem template

2026-02-23 — Carlos Mendes (review): Proposed SLI definitions look good. Requested we prefer p95 over p99 for the 'queued duration' SLI to reduce alert noise; accepted. Also suggested adding tenant-cardinality tag to all ingest spans for correlation.

2026-02-28 — Anika Sharma: Prototype PR opened for trace signature capture and small similarity scorer (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/compare/feature/trace-signatures). Includes unit tests and a small benchmark (see PR comment).

2026-03-03 — QA: Ran synthetic probe against staging for 48h. Observed two false positives when there was planned scaling activity. Note: need to suppress alerts for planned autoscale windows or add scale-event annotation to synthetic traces.
2026-03-08 — Design review (PM + Oncall): Decided on the 4 golden signatures and canonical span naming. PM asked for a short explainer card to attach to the dashboard for SRE onboarding.
2026-03-10 — Anika Sharma: Merged PR for trace tag propagation and sampling config. Next: finalize Grafana dashboard panels and create runbook draft.
notes: Design tradeoffs considered: aggressive trace sampling gives better fidelity for signature matching but increases cost; decided on adaptive sampling for 10% baseline + 80% on error traces.

Operational concern: high-cardinality tenant tags will increase index cardinality in our trace store. Mitigation: create sampled tenant hash (tenant_id_low) for dashboards and store full tenant_id only on error traces.
Metrics queries provided are intended for the current metrics backend (Prometheus/remote write). If we migrate metric backends, update the query spec in the SLI doc.
